targetNetwork.fact: Europe ran about 100 night train lines in 2025 — roughly what you are planning here.
targetNetwork.demand: 300 lines by 2035, enough to triple the number of night train passengers.

sevenInTen.fact: 7 in 10 Europeans say they would take a night train instead of a plane, given reasonable conditions.
sevenInTen.demand: dominant booking platforms to be required to show every night train running in their country.

euEmissions.fact: A comprehensive European night train network could avoid 3% of the EU's total greenhouse gas emissions.
euEmissions.demand: the Connecting Europe Facility — nearly €40 billion over six years — to co-finance night train coaches and track access charges.

aviation.fact: Moving travellers from planes to night trains could cut about a quarter of aviation emissions.
aviation.demand: a minimum airline ticket price, to stop fares being dumped below cost.

climate.fact: Taking a night train is about 30 times better for the climate than flying the same route.
climate.demand: VAT scrapped on international rail tickets — international flights are already taxed at 0%.

europeanSleeper.fact: European Sleeper's Brussels–Berlin–Prague route carried more than 230,000 passengers on over 750 trains in its first year.
europeanSleeper.demand: the EU to buy sleeper and couchette coaches and lease them out, so newcomers like this one carry less risk.

flyLess.fact: Nearly half of surveyed night train passengers say they will fly less and take the train more over the next five years.
flyLess.demand: night trains prioritised when train paths are allocated, so the services people want can actually run.

carpatia.fact: Since December 2025 the Carpatia sleeper has linked Przemyśl and Kraków with Vienna, Salzburg and Munich.
carpatia.demand: EU co-funding for pilot routes to Europe's edges — Portugal, Greece, the Nordics, the Baltics.

parisBerlin.fact: A Paris–Brussels–Berlin sleeper has run since March 2026, and Brussels–Milan is due to follow.
parisBerlin.demand: closed border stations reopened — no passenger train has crossed between Irun and Hendaye since 2020.

rollingStock.fact: Europe has roughly 1,500 night train carriages. A full network needs several thousand more by 2035.
rollingStock.demand: the European Investment Bank's Green Rail Investment Platform actually funded — the budget line is still empty.

reuse.fact: About 1,300 publicly funded carriages are being scrapped in France, while Europe is short of sleeper stock.
reuse.demand: EU rules that make reusing second-hand rolling stock possible instead.

network.fact: Back-on-Track is a volunteer network of around 60 active members, with groups in eleven European countries.
network.demand: night trains treated as their own transport segment, exempt from track access surcharges.

welcome.lead: Europe was once crossed by night trains. We want them back.
welcome.body: Back-on-Track is building the Target Network 2032: a map of the night train connections Europe needs, which we'll ask the EU to support. Every route runs on tracks that already exist — nothing new has to be built.
